task: Document the new `edits` parameter of the `update_document` MCP tool. The implementation is in cli/internal/mcp/tools/update_document.go (see NewUpdateDocumentTool, HandleUpdateDocument, parseEdits, applyEdits) and its test TestHandleUpdateDocument_Edits in cli/internal/mcp/tools/update_document_test.go. Read the code before you state behavior.
context: Measured in the maintainer's Claude Code transcripts (2676 write calls): tool execution takes about 0.1 s for create_document, update_document, Write, and Edit; model generation takes about 4 s per 1000 characters for every tool. Generation, not the tool, is the cost.
In 410 update_document calls with a known previous body, the median share of the new body copied unchanged was 91%; across all of them only 13% of generated characters were new.
279 of 448 content updates targeted a document created earlier in the same session: fix iterations after create_document, often after a [Archcore Precision] hook advisory.

Alternative considered and not taken: allow native Write/Edit on .archcore/ with post-write validation. It conflicts with the accepted decision .archcore/plugin/always-use-mcp-tools.adr.md, whose alternative 2 rejected direct writes for updates.

The draft spec .archcore/mcp/document-update-frontmatter.spec.md still lists the supported update arguments as title, status, tags, and content; it needs a follow-up update, which is out of scope for this package.
Plugin skills do not mention edits yet; agents learn about it from the tool description.

docs.title: update_document Accepts Exact-Match edits Instead of a Full-Body Rewrite
docs.intent: Record the decision to add the edits parameter, the measured context, the rejected native Write/Edit alternative, and the consequences.

docs.title: update_document edits Contract
docs.intent: Normative contract of the edits parameter: argument shape, ordered application, exactly-once match, all-or-nothing write, mutual exclusion with content, error behavior.

docs.title: Fixing a Document With update_document edits
docs.intent: Actor-subject flows and Given/When/Then examples that illustrate the spec clauses: a precision fix after create_document, an ambiguous old_string, a not-found old_string.

docs.title: Partial Document Changes Use update_document edits
docs.intent: Agent rule: when an agent changes part of an existing document body it uses edits, and it uses content only for a full rewrite.
